metodo.titulo: First I write down how I'll check it.
metodo.sub: Generating code is cheap now. Below is the part I do, each with a real example.
metodo.agencia.texto: I write the brief, the flow and the quality bar before I ask an agent for a single line. I also decide what stays out.
metodo.agencia.ejemplo: Fortal: the training rules (double progression, volume by available time, weights you can actually load) were written before the first screen.
metodo.juicio.texto: I accept it, fix it or send it back with the reason in writing. When there are alternatives, I pick one and note why.
metodo.juicio.ejemplo: coro: I ruled out ranking complaints by count and measured concentration instead. When a single topic holds 47 % of the complaints, that's a defect.
metodo.orquestacion.texto: Every batch ends in automated tests and full-resolution screenshots. Something is done when I've seen it rendered.
metodo.orquestacion.ejemplo: Cathedra: over 5,500 automated tests. Fortal: 746, and every phase verified with 1206×2622 screenshots, one by one.
metodo.confio.titulo: When I trust it and when I redo it
metodo.confio.texto: I trust an output when the test passes and the screenshot matches the brief. If I can't explain how it got to that result, I redo it, even if it works.
sobre.titulo: I was the first user of both Cathedra and Fortal.
sobre.texto: Ramiro Bales. I build my own products from idea to release: I write the brief, direct the AI agents that write the code and check what they deliver. I'm also studying for a degree in AI and Data Science at UADE. Native Spanish, English B2 (Duolingo English Test). I'm looking for remote work as an AI Product Builder, in AI automation or as a creative technologist.

sobre.busco.2: AI product: defining, designing and verifying what gets built.

sobre.busco.4: Creative technology: real-time 3D and interactive websites.

marcas.titulo: Three demos with a benefit you can measure.
marcas.sub: Built with the same method as my products. Ámbar Muebles is a fictional brand created for these demos, and so is the club in the bot room. Third-party figures cite their source; the bot figure is my own measurement.
marcas.config.alt: Velvet armchair with walnut wood and brass buttons, in the demo 3D configurator
marcas.config.resuelve: The customer rotates the piece, switches fabric, wood and metal, and sees the price instantly, on a phone and with nothing to install.
marcas.config.gana: Fewer doubts before buying: texture, scale and finish are visible before paying, so there are fewer "it wasn't what I expected" moments.
marcas.config.cifra: Up to twice the conversion on product pages with 3D and augmented reality.
marcas.config.fuente: Threekit, guide to ROI in 3D and AR (Shopify data)
marcas.asis.titulo: A catalogue assistant that doesn't make things up
marcas.asis.resuelve: It answers pre-sale questions (sizes, lead times, care) citing the product sheet; if the fact is missing, it says so and hands over to a person with a summary.
marcas.asis.gana: Repeated tickets go down, everyone gets the same answer, every answer can be audited and customers still get help after hours.
marcas.asis.cifra: 20% lower average cost in companies that automate; high-volume, rules-based processes pay off the most.
marcas.asis.fuente: Bain & Company, cited by Zapier in its guide to automating a business
metodo.esquema.1: I write down what hurts, for whom, and how we'll know it's solved.
metodo.esquema.2: The flow, the quality bar and the acceptance criteria are on paper before I ask for a single line.
metodo.esquema.3: They work in small batches, each with its own brief, its tests and the screenshots it has to deliver.
metodo.esquema.4: I run the tests and look at the screenshots at full resolution. Anything that doesn't match goes back to step 3 with the reason.

caso.cathedra.descripcion: Cathedra, a Windows study app in beta: it transcribes lectures, builds the plan, generates exams and flashcards, and every answer cites the lecture and the timestamp. How I defined it, directed it with AI agents and verified it.
caso.cathedra.gancho: From hours of recorded lectures to a study plan where every answer cites the lecture and the timestamp.
caso.cathedra.resumen.1: A Windows study app: it transcribes your lectures and builds the guide, the mock exam and the flashcards from them.
caso.cathedra.resumen.2: University students with recorded lectures and course material.
caso.cathedra.resumen.3: Beta 1.2.0, with an installer for Windows 10 and 11 and a public page.
caso.cathedra.rol: Founder and product builder. I defined the product, the six-step flow, the identity and the quality bar; I directed development and verified every task.
caso.cathedra.herramientas: AI-assisted development · Python · HTML, CSS and JavaScript · local transcription · embedding retrieval
caso.cathedra.resultado: Beta 1.2.0 published, with a Windows installer and a public page.
caso.cathedra.reflexion.1: Settle the identity before building screens; redoing it twice meant rebuilding screens that were already done.
caso.cathedra.galeria.aviso: Screenshots use demo data: fictional subjects, lecturers and student.
caso.cathedra.hace.1: Recorded lectures of up to 4 hours, with an anti-hallucination check; the transcript is good enough that you never need to rewatch the lecture.
caso.cathedra.hace.2: Classifies every piece of material as content, exam, practical work or course logistics.
caso.cathedra.hace.7: Explaining the topic in your own words to check you understood it.
caso.cathedra.hace.8: Compares what was covered with the official syllabus and shows what's still missing.
caso.cathedra.hace.10: A cloud engine or a four-layer local engine: language, rules, embedding retrieval and symbolic maths.
caso.cathedra.hace.11: Read-aloud and audio summaries: the class in 5 minutes.
caso.cathedra.hace.12: A graphing calculator, 3D concept scenes, memory games and Telegram reminders.
caso.cathedra.decision.1.vi: A student can't tell a fluent explanation from an invention.
caso.cathedra.decision.1.elegi: Every answer carries the lecture, the timestamp and who said it, and the citation tag stays empty if the fact isn't in the material.
caso.cathedra.decision.1.porque: If it can't be traced back to the lecturer, it's no use for studying.
caso.cathedra.decision.2.vi: In a single class the lecturer mixes content with notes about the exam and the course.
caso.cathedra.decision.2.elegi: Classify every block as content, exam, practical work or course logistics, and build a single plan per subject.
caso.cathedra.decision.2.porque: With several plans you don't know which to follow; with one plan fed by everything, you do.
caso.cathedra.decision.3.vi: The lectures belong to the student and the connection isn't always good.
caso.cathedra.decision.3.elegi: Transcribe and store on the computer, with a local engine that works without internet.
caso.cathedra.decision.3.descarte: Depending only on a cloud service.
caso.cathedra.decision.3.porque: Studying can't stop because the connection drops.
caso.cathedra.agentes.1: The six steps order the app and its page (start, upload, it reads, ask, sit the exam, review), and one rule governs them: nothing that isn't in the material.
caso.cathedra.agentes.2.t: One scoped task at a time.
caso.cathedra.agentes.2: Each feature was its own task, with a brief, acceptance criteria, required screenshots and a single agent responsible for it.
caso.cathedra.agentes.3: Before calling anything "final", a separate review checks the front end and the back end: copy, buttons and measured contrast in the light theme.
caso.cathedra.agentes.4: Full-resolution screenshots, checked one by one, and over 5,500 automated tests.
caso.cathedra.agentes.5: The identity, twice: the first palette (black and light blue) went, and leather, ivory, glass and cherry stayed; the emblem was redone until the material read as real.

caso.fortal.descripcion: Fortal, an iPhone web app that builds the routine from your real gear and time on a 3D body. Personal app, published and in daily use.
caso.fortal.gancho: A routine built from the gear and the time you actually have, and one I use every day.
caso.fortal.resumen.1: An installable iPhone web app that builds the day's routine on a 3D model of the body.
caso.fortal.resumen.2: Anyone training with their own gear and little time; today, me.
caso.fortal.resumen.3: Published and in daily use; a personal app, not in the stores.
caso.fortal.herramientas: AI-assisted development · React and TypeScript · Three.js · PWA · IndexedDB · Web Push
caso.fortal.enlace: No public link: single-user app, shown with screenshots
caso.fortal.cabecera.alt: Chest muscle card on the Fortal 3D body: 100% recovery, rank and sets this week
caso.fortal.resultado: Published and installed on my iPhone; I use it every day.
caso.fortal.reflexion.1: Separate the profile from the code from day one; today it's hard-wired, which is why there is no public link.
caso.fortal.reflexion.2: Opening it to other people would require accounts and onboarding.
caso.fortal.hace.3: Computes plates per side, dumbbell dial and weight stack with the gear at hand.
caso.fortal.hace.6: A search over about 350 foods, free text ("2 eggs and 150 g of rice") and notifications.
caso.fortal.decision.1.vi: A weight suggestion you can't load in the gym is noise.
caso.fortal.decision.1.elegi: Compute the weights from the real gear: plates per side, dumbbell dial, weight stack.
caso.fortal.decision.1.descarte: Asking for the weight by hand.
caso.fortal.decision.1.porque: It forces you to do the maths mid-set.
caso.fortal.decision.2.vi: A list of exercises doesn't show which muscle was left untrained.
caso.fortal.decision.2.elegi: A 3D body with twenty regions painted by what's due today and by recovery.
caso.fortal.decision.2.descarte: A table of sets per muscle.
caso.fortal.decision.2.porque: The body reads at a glance; the table has to be studied.
caso.fortal.decision.3.vi: The only user was me and I wanted to iterate every day.
caso.fortal.decision.3.elegi: A web app installable from Safari, local first and offline.
caso.fortal.decision.3.porque: With no store review and no mandatory server, every change ships the same day.
caso.fortal.agentes.1: The training and nutrition rules (double progression, volume by available time, safety without safety bars) were written before the first screen.
caso.fortal.agentes.2: Gym, routine, live session, food: one phase at a time, each with its brief and measured against those rules.
caso.fortal.agentes.3: A model with twenty muscle regions went through my own pipeline down to a light GLB.
caso.fortal.agentes.4: Screenshots at 1206×2622, the iPhone resolution, checked one by one; 391 unit tests, 85 server tests and 270 end-to-end tests as a safety net.
caso.fortal.agentes.5: I pixelated the body data in the screenshots: weight and measurements aren't published.
caso.fortal.galeria.2: Ranks view: triceps at Bronce II, marked on the 3D body
caso.fortal.galeria.3: The week as planned: Legs A, Shoulders and traps, Upper B and Legs B, with minutes and sets
caso.fortal.galeria.4: Live session: log a set, failure, drop and rest-pause, exercises with weight and reps

caso.athleteiq.descripcion: AthleteIQ, a prototype chat bot for a rugby league coaching staff: you ask by text, voice note or photo and it answers from each player's record. Demo landing page in five languages.
caso.athleteiq.gancho: The staff asks about a player from the touchline, and the bot answers from that player's record.
caso.athleteiq.resumen.1: A chat bot that answers questions about the squad from each player's record, by text, voice note or photo.
caso.athleteiq.resumen.2: Strength and conditioning coaches and coaching staff at professional clubs; the demo is built for rugby league.
caso.athleteiq.resumen.3: Prototype with a working demo: a landing page in five languages and test chat bots. No clients or contracts.
caso.athleteiq.herramientas: AI-assisted development · Three.js · Telegram API · HTML, CSS and JavaScript
caso.athleteiq.enlace: Landing page mock-up, with a generic club and made-up names
caso.athleteiq.resultado: Landing page and bots working as a demo, with no clients or contracts.
caso.athleteiq.reflexion.1: Build it generic from the start; tying it to a real club meant cleaning it up before I could show it.
caso.athleteiq.galeria.aviso: Screenshots of the demo landing page: generic club and made-up player names.
caso.athleteiq.hace.3: Besides text, it takes voice notes and photos.
caso.athleteiq.hace.5: A 3D rugby ball built with Three.js and a scripted chat with four questions.
caso.athleteiq.decision.1.vi: The staff makes decisions on the field, phone in hand.
caso.athleteiq.decision.1.elegi: Chat bots that answer in plain language.
caso.athleteiq.decision.1.porque: Nobody opens a dashboard between two drills.
caso.athleteiq.decision.2.vi: An international coaching staff doesn't work in a single language.
caso.athleteiq.decision.2.elegi: Reply in the language each question is asked in, and write the landing page in five (EN, ES, PT, FR, ZH).
caso.athleteiq.decision.2.porque: Coaches should ask the way they think, without translating first.
caso.athleteiq.decision.3.vi: Without a contract, someone else's name or an assumed figure reads as a promise.
caso.athleteiq.decision.3.elegi: Show the demo with a generic club and made-up player names, and no return figures.
caso.athleteiq.decision.3.descarte: Publishing the version tied to a real club.
caso.athleteiq.decision.3.porque: What hasn't been measured isn't shown as a result.
caso.athleteiq.agentes.1: First the message (“The Data Has No Favourites”) and the questions a staff would really ask; the screens came after.
caso.athleteiq.agentes.2: Dark, with the 3D ball surrounded by the fields of the player record; five languages from translation files.
caso.athleteiq.agentes.3: They answer by text, voice and photo, in the user's language, about the squad.
caso.athleteiq.agentes.4: Landing page captured at 1920×1080; bots that take text, voice notes and photos.
caso.athleteiq.agentes.5: To publish it I removed the real club, the players, the access to the bots and the assumed figures; the demo on this site is that cleaned-up copy.
caso.athleteiq.galeria.1: The “How it works” section of the landing page: you write or send a voice note, the bot reads the records, answers with a recommendation, and what is missing
caso.athleteiq.galeria.1.pie: “How it works”, on the landing page: the fourth step says what is still missing.
caso.coro.descripcion: coro reads a product's public reviews, groups the recurring defect and looks for who already fixed it: a competitor, a supplier or a patent, with its source. Prototype with an HTML report.
caso.coro.gancho: From hundreds of reviews to one concrete defect and who already fixed it.
caso.coro.resumen.1: A tool that reads a product's public reviews, groups the recurring defect and looks for who already fixed it, with the source: a competitor, a supplier or a patent.
caso.coro.resumen.2: Shoppers, resellers and manufacturers: four profiles read the same report, each with its own question.
caso.coro.resumen.3: A command-line prototype that generates one HTML report per product.
caso.coro.rol: I defined the product, the profiles, the deciding metric, the rule on solutions and the report format; I directed development and validated it.
caso.coro.herramientas: AI-assisted development · Node.js · ES modules · static HTML report
caso.coro.resultado: A command-line prototype that generates the HTML report for a product.
caso.coro.apoyo: It runs on a product's reviews or on a local test set. No users or clients.
caso.coro.reflexion.1: Publish a sample report as a page from the start; today there are only screenshots.
caso.coro.reflexion.2: It runs from the command line, so a brand can't use it on its own yet.
caso.coro.galeria.aviso: Sample report on the test fixture: the topics, their reviews and the solution were loaded by hand; coro computes concentration, priority and the break date. Suppliers renamed generically.
caso.coro.hace.1: A product's public reviews: 400 in the largest real run and 1,200 in a load test.
caso.coro.hace.6: Consumer, small online reseller, brand buying from a third party and brand that manufactures.
caso.coro.decision.1.vi: Twenty topics with five complaints aren't a defect; one with 47% is.
caso.coro.decision.1.elegi: Measure concentration: what share of the negatives points at the same thing.
caso.coro.decision.1.porque: Counting rewards the most talked-about topic, not the defect that keeps coming back.
caso.coro.decision.2.vi: An invented solution reads as confidently as a real one.
caso.coro.decision.2.elegi: Solutions are searched for and cited with a source, and the report says when there is no evidence.
caso.coro.decision.2.porque: A "not found" is worth more than an invented solution.
caso.coro.decision.3.vi: The same complaint means different things to the person who buys and to the company that manufactures.
caso.coro.decision.3.elegi: One report with four readings: consumer, small online reseller, brand buying from a third party and brand that manufactures.
caso.coro.decision.3.porque: "Should I buy it?" and "what do I claim from my supplier?" aren't answered by the same paragraph.
caso.coro.agentes.1: The profiles and the metric were defined before the code: concentration, by severity, weighted up if the topic is growing.
caso.coro.agentes.2: Analysis, quality, history, profiles, solutions and report, each with its acceptance criteria.
caso.coro.agentes.4: I ran it on 400 real reviews in the largest run and on 1,200 in a load test; as a test case I used a 32-review test fixture for a filtered shower head, and I checked the rendered report.
caso.coro.agentes.5: In a copy of the report I replaced real stores and suppliers with generic names.

saber.1.1: A watcher that spots a new recorded lecture, transcribes it, files it under its subject and archives it.
saber.1.2: A connector that downloads lecture recordings from Teams on its own.
saber.1.3: Releasing a version in one command, with a guard that stops if it finds keys or personal paths.
saber.1.4: A Windows installer in two editions: full and light.
saber.1.5: Loading sources into NotebookLM notebooks with deduplication and content checks: 358 sources loaded.
saber.1.6: A review analyser that checks the sample before spending on the analysis.
saber.2.1: A Telegram bot that answers text, photos and transcribed voice notes, with per-chat history and a usage limit.
saber.2.2: Reminders for exams and deadlines, generated from the course calendar.
saber.2.3: A prototype daily brief of industry news and an opportunity radar that drops repeats, both scheduled.
saber.2.4: Workout push notifications on the iPhone.
saber.2.5: Oral exams and a voice assistant.
saber.2.6: Incoming message handling with deduplication and caching, in Apps Script.
saber.3.1: Local transcription of lectures up to 4 hours long, with the option chosen by measuring on my own graphics card.
saber.3.2: Local language engine, embedding retrieval and synthetic voice, all offline.
saber.3.3: Answers that cite the lecture and the timestamp; when something isn't in the material, the answer says so.
saber.3.4: Exams, flashcards and games generated from the material, and a simulated student who studies for a week to measure quality.
saber.3.5: Splitting the work between models by cost and quality.
saber.3.6: A fraud-detection agent with logistic regression: 83.3% accuracy against 33.3% and 66.7% for the baselines; graded 10/10.
saber.4.1: A local server that listens only on its own machine and, on top of that, checks the Origin header and blocks path traversal.
saber.4.2: CSP and passwords hashed with scrypt and salt, with an attempt cap and atomic writes.
saber.4.3: Codes stored as hashes with a per-minute limit, and the user's key encrypted with DPAPI.
saber.4.4: Proxies without SSRF, a size cap and a required credential on every route, with tests.
saber.4.5: Legal and privacy research before the beta: terms, AI notice and which data leaves the device.
saber.4.6: Risk analysis based on expected cost.
saber.5.1: A complete brand identity: leather, ivory, glass and cherry, with a layered 3D emblem.
saber.5.2: 23 Blender scripts rendering backgrounds, icons and atlases in Cycles, with PBR materials and real textures.
saber.5.3: Liquid glass with refraction, and light and dark themes with contrast measured on pixels.
saber.5.4: A hologram shader with bloom and a 3D body with labelled muscles.
saber.5.5: Real-time Three.js scene that responds to clicks.
saber.5.6: Sound signatures mastered to −18 LUFS, and reduced motion respected.
saber.6.1: A desktop app with WebView2 and a local server with streaming.
saber.6.2: A local-first PWA that works offline, with Web Push and Workbox, in React 19 and TypeScript.
saber.6.3: A two-sided marketplace in production: Next.js, Postgres with 27 migrations, accounts, messaging and contracts.
saber.6.4: A 3D landing page in five languages.
saber.6.5: Exporting a store mock-up with 3D to Shopify.
saber.6.6: Deployments on Vercel, Cloudflare and Netlify.
saber.7.1: Postgres with migrations and seed data.
saber.7.2: Logistic regression with leave-one-out validation and baselines.
saber.7.3: Backtests and simulation without look-ahead bias, with news stored at the real time it arrived: 543 queries with measured cost.
saber.7.4: Connections to exchanges and prediction markets.

caso.cathedra.problema.titulo: A recorded lecture can run four hours, and the explanation the exam depends on sits somewhere in that audio.
caso.cathedra.problema.texto: Add several subjects like that, plus the course readings, and nobody knows what the exam covers or where each topic was explained. Rewatching everything doesn't scale, and a generic assistant answers just as confidently when the fact isn't in the material.
caso.cathedra.recorrido.titulo: Everything comes from the lectures you upload: the plan, the guide, the mock exam and the review.
caso.cathedra.recorrido.1.t: One plan per subject, built from the course calendar
caso.cathedra.recorrido.1: You upload the calendar as a PDF, a Word file or a photo, and it sets up subjects, lectures, dates and exams. Anything the calendar leaves out is flagged, never guessed. The home screen shows the next step and how many days are left for each deadline.
caso.cathedra.recorrido.2.t: Each lecture becomes a guide you read block by block
caso.cathedra.recorrido.2: The recording is transcribed on the computer, offline too, and turned into a guide per lecture and per topic. Every block keeps the sentence and the minute it came from. At the top, the lecture summed up in five minutes of audio.
caso.cathedra.recorrido.3.t: The mock exam is built from what the lecturer said would be on it
caso.cathedra.recorrido.3: The app pulls what was said about the exam out of the lecture content and gathers it under “How it will be assessed”, each sentence with its lecture and minute. The mock exam follows that format, and the marking shows where each question came from.
caso.cathedra.recorrido.4.t: What you got wrong comes back before the exam
caso.cathedra.recorrido.4: Mistakes, games and flashcards go into one review deck. You rate each card from “again” to “easy”, and “How much per day” spreads what's left until each exam date.

caso.cathedra.firma.titulo: Every answer can be traced back to the minute the lecturer said it.
caso.cathedra.firma.texto: The answer keeps three things apart: what the app explains, an example of its own labelled “the lecturer didn't say this”, and the lecturer's exact words, with the lecture and a button to minute 14:20 of the recording. If the fact isn't in the material, the citation stays empty and the app offers to search elsewhere.

caso.fortal.problema.titulo: The routine lived in my phone's notes, and the weight was a guess in the middle of every set.
caso.fortal.problema.texto: Gym apps don't know what gear you have at home or how much time each day really leaves. They suggest weights you can't load with the plates you own, and they don't show which muscle went untrained. I wanted to open my phone and see what's due today, how long it takes and with what weight.
caso.fortal.recorrido.titulo: From the days, minutes and gear available, it builds the week and highlights today's muscles on the body.
caso.fortal.recorrido.aviso: Real screenshots from my iPhone, with training times and body data pixelated.
caso.fortal.recorrido.1.t: The week is built around the minutes each day really has
caso.fortal.recorrido.1: You pick days, minutes and intensity, and it builds the week from a template or from scratch. Each day lists the muscles it works, how many sets it has and how long it runs against the time you have: on Wednesday, 72 of 75 minutes.
caso.fortal.recorrido.2.t: Tap a muscle to see whether it has recovered
caso.fortal.recorrido.2: Each of the body's twenty regions opens its own card: recovery, rank, sets this week and when it's due again. The chest in the screenshot is at 100%, ready to train, and comes up on Friday.
caso.fortal.recorrido.3.t: Each muscle climbs through ranks as it progresses
caso.fortal.recorrido.3: The Ranks view paints each muscle's level on the body, on a scale from bronze up to “Mano de Dios” (Hand of God). In the screenshot, the triceps sit at Bronce II and the forearms at Bronce IV.

The first carries three times more than any other, and a real run on the same test fixture also gave it 47.4%. The solution is an example loaded by hand to show how the report cites its source.

caso.coro.hace.8: Keeps every run and raises the priority of a topic that is growing.
caso.coro.problema.texto: Shoppers, resellers and manufacturers have no time to read them all, and no way to know whether someone already fixed that defect. The star average doesn't help either: it can't tell a concentrated, fixable defect from a product with scattered complaints.
caso.coro.problema.titulo: Reviews about the same failure get buried under complaints about everything else.
caso.coro.recorrido.1: The metric that decides is concentration: what share of the negative reviews point at the same thing. Next to it sit the average rating, the share of three-star-or-lower reviews and how many topics it found.
caso.coro.recorrido.1.alt: The sample report’s verdict in an amber band and four metrics for the test product
caso.coro.recorrido.1.prueba: With a 32-review test fixture for a filtered shower head, a real run grouped 47.4% of the negative reviews into one topic, the same share as the sample report in the screenshots.
caso.coro.recorrido.1.t: The verdict says first whether there is a defect or just scattered complaints
caso.coro.recorrido.2: When a topic barely appears before a certain date and is steady after it, the report flags it as new: it usually means a change of batch, supplier or process. Below it comes the likely root cause, labelled as a hypothesis.
caso.coro.recorrido.2.alt: Topic 1 of the report: flagged as a new topic with the date it started, and the root-cause hypothesis
caso.coro.recorrido.2.t: If a complaint started on a certain date, the report gives you the date
caso.coro.recorrido.3: Quotes are verbatim, with stars, date and whether the purchase was verified; in the screenshots they come from the test fixture. Anyone reading the report can check the topic without going back to the store.
caso.coro.recorrido.3.alt: Four verbatim quotes from the test fixture, each with its star rating, date and verified-purchase mark
caso.coro.recorrido.3.t: Each topic comes with its reviews, word for word
caso.coro.recorrido.4: Solutions are searched for and cited with their source. When no public evidence turns up, the report says so, and notes it could be an opening or a search that missed the source. In the sample report, that topic had no solution loaded.
caso.coro.recorrido.4.alt: Topic 2 of the report, a leak at the connection: quotes and, under “Who already fixed it”, a note that no public evidence was found
caso.coro.recorrido.4.t: When nobody has fixed it, the report says exactly that
caso.coro.recorrido.titulo: A report you read top to bottom: the verdict, the cause, the proof and the fix.

caso.chamfer.problema.titulo: A small store builds its product page from the editor's blocks, and next to the brand it admires it looks flat.
caso.chamfer.problema.texto: The theme editor handles the basics well: photo, title, price and button. Its blocks show the photo flat, with no turntable, no exploded view and no close-up of the material, and the merchant has no 3D models of the product to build them. The other way out is paying a developer for a single page.

caso.prospeccion.titulo: Verified outreach — case study · Ramiro Bales
caso.prospeccion.gancho: An AI model drafts the first email. A checker with no AI decides whether it goes out.
caso.prospeccion.resumen.1: An engine that finds small businesses with their own website, measures what their site is missing and drafts a first email.
caso.prospeccion.resumen.2: My own use: writing to a small business with one improvement measured on its website.
caso.prospeccion.resumen.3: Prototype. By 11 November 2026 it had sent 6 real emails, capped at 5 a day.
caso.prospeccion.rol.corto: I set the rules and directed the build
caso.prospeccion.herramientas: AI-assisted development · Python · SQLite · OpenStreetMap · SMTP sending
caso.prospeccion.problema.titulo: If an email tells a business its site has no WhatsApp button, that button had better really be missing.
caso.prospeccion.problema.texto: I wanted to write to small businesses with one concrete improvement for their website, and have an AI model draft the first email. A model sounds just as sure about what was measured as about what wasn't. The emails go out without me reading each one first, so the rule had to live in the code.
caso.prospeccion.lector.t: If you got an email from this engine
caso.prospeccion.lector: An AI model wrote it from what the audit measured on your website, and the checker approved it: nobody read it before it was sent. The engine won't write to the same contact again within 120 days. If you reply "STOP", your address and your domain are removed for good.
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.titulo: An AI model writes in exactly one step. Everything else is code with written rules.
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.aviso: Excerpts copied from the engine's code, unchanged.
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.1.pie: The sentence comes from the code, in both languages, and the model has to copy it word for word.
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.1.t: Every measurement becomes a fixed sentence
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.1: The audit reads the homepage and up to two contact pages. It looks for chat or WhatsApp, booking, a store, https, mobile support, the footer year and the search description. Each gap becomes a fixed sentence.
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.2.pie: The pattern highlighted on line 21 keeps the comma or full stop that follows a number. In the 11 November run, that bug stopped five drafts.
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.2.t: No number goes out unless the audit measured it
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.2: The checker uses no AI. It compares each draft with the audit and stops it if it claims a gap nobody measured, uses an unsupported number or a percentage, promises results or asks for a call.
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.2.prueba: In the 11 November run the checker made 16 checks on real drafts: 11 approved, 5 stopped. All five were false positives, explained further down.
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.3.pie: The sending settings the engine used.
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.3.t: The sending limits are written down and the code enforces them
caso.prospeccion.recorrido.3: Up to 5 emails a day and 30 a week, Monday to Friday between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. in the recipient's time zone, and 120 days before writing to the same contact again. With the pause switched on, nothing goes out.
caso.prospeccion.hace.1.t: Only businesses with their own website
caso.prospeccion.hace.1: Social profiles and directories don't count as a website; large institutions and branded chains are skipped.
caso.prospeccion.hace.2: Each business is stored with its domain as the key.
caso.prospeccion.hace.3: In the United States it doesn't write to clinics or dentists, because they handle health data.
caso.prospeccion.hace.4.t: It identifies itself and backs off
caso.prospeccion.hace.4: The audit announces itself as a bot, with a name and an address, and if a site blocks it, it doesn't try again.
caso.prospeccion.hace.5.t: Sender details and opt-out in every email
caso.prospeccion.hace.5: Name, role, website, postal address, where the email address was found, a commercial notice and how to opt out, plus a List-Unsubscribe header.
caso.prospeccion.hace.6: An opt-out removes that address and its domain for good, and the checker looks it up before approving anything.
caso.prospeccion.detalle.pie: Lines from the checker’s log: the “unsupported number” reason and the time each draft went out rewritten.
caso.prospeccion.firma.titulo: By 11 November: 57 businesses found, 16 drafts checked, 6 emails sent.
caso.prospeccion.embudo.t: Per business, stage by stage, as of 11 November 2026
caso.prospeccion.registro.cuando: All five were stopped at 15:23 and approved at 15:24 once rewritten. 11 November 2026, UTC.
caso.prospeccion.firma.nota: Numbers read from the engine’s database, counted per business. Original in Spanish, as the engine logs it; translation below.
caso.prospeccion.firma.texto: Each stage counts distinct businesses: one audited twice counts once. In the 11 November run, all five reasons in the log share the same shape, a number with a comma stuck to it. The checker read "500," or "240," and didn't match it to the supported figure. The five drafts were rewritten and went out the same day.
caso.prospeccion.firma.pie: The real view, generated from the database with no names, emails, domains or cities.
caso.prospeccion.decisiones.titulo: What an email nobody checks by hand is allowed to claim.
caso.prospeccion.decision.1.elegi: A checker with no AI and written rules gets the last word on every draft.
caso.prospeccion.decision.1.vi: The emails go out without me reading each one, and a model sounds just as sure about what it measured as about what it made up.
caso.prospeccion.decision.1.descarte: Having a second model review the first.
caso.prospeccion.decision.1.porque: A written rule can be read and audited line by line.
caso.prospeccion.decision.2.elegi: The engine doesn't claim anything it can't measure reliably.
caso.prospeccion.decision.2.vi: On Windows, Python's certificate check reports errors that aren't there, and a chat loaded through Google Tag Manager doesn't show up in the HTML.
caso.prospeccion.decision.2.descarte: Telling a business its certificate is broken.
caso.prospeccion.decision.2.porque: So that sentence is never sent, and a missing chat on a site that uses Google Tag Manager isn't enough reason to write.
caso.prospeccion.decision.3.elegi: When a number looks doubtful, the checker stops the draft, even if it turns out to be wrong.
caso.prospeccion.decision.3.vi: In the 11 November run it stopped 5 of 16 checks and all five were false positives: it read "500," or "240," with the comma attached and didn't match them to the supported figures.
caso.prospeccion.decision.3.descarte: Loosening the rule so close-enough numbers get through.
caso.prospeccion.decision.3.porque: A draft stopped by mistake gets rewritten; an email with a false number is already out. The parsing bug is still there.
caso.prospeccion.construi.titulo: An automated pipeline, tested in draft mode before it sent anything.
caso.prospeccion.agentes.1.t: I split what the code does from what the model does.
caso.prospeccion.agentes.1: A first pass discovers, audits and prepares. The closing pass composes, checks, sends, reads the inbox and builds the dashboard. In between sits the only AI step: drafting, from written instructions.
caso.prospeccion.construi.artefacto.1: The steps as they are named in the engine. The fourth, highlighted, is the only one that uses an AI model. Original in Spanish; translation below.
caso.prospeccion.agentes.2: In draft mode the engine builds the full email and saves it without sending. That is how 5 approved drafts ended up never going out.
caso.prospeccion.agentes.3.t: A view that exposes no one.
caso.prospeccion.agentes.3: The funnel view is built from the database opened read-only. The script refuses to write it if it finds an @, a domain, or any name, city or email address stored in the database.
caso.prospeccion.resultado: A prototype that has already sent real emails, with a daily cap and no business results to report.

caso.prospeccion.falta.1: Fix how numbers are parsed: today a comma or a full stop right after a number stops the whole draft.
caso.prospeccion.falta.2: Detect chats loaded through Google Tag Manager: today the audit can miss them and only lowers the weight of that finding.
caso.prospeccion.falta.3: Turn on the mobile speed check: it is off, so that finding never appears.

caso.cathedra.firma.traduccion: In English: “Why aren’t Didone typefaces used for newspaper body text?” How the lecturer put it: “but at small sizes the thin strokes disappear, they break up, especially if they print on cheap paper. that’s why they aren’t used for newspaper text.” Lecture 2, minute 14:20.
caso.fortal.firma.traduccion: In English: Today: Arms and abs. Light day: biceps, triceps and core (biceps, triceps, abs, forearms). Live session: 2 cable triceps extension, 3 hammer curl, 4 overhead dumbbell extension, 5 high-cable crunch; each with sets × reps, RIR 1, last set to failure, rest and the suggested weight.
caso.coro.firma.traduccion: In English: Verdict: “Single, fixable defect — 47.4% of the negative reviews point to the same thing.” Topics: the head can’t be opened to change the filter (47.4%); water leaking at the connection (15.8%); perceived pressure drop (15.8%); billing and cancelling the filter subscription (15.8%). Who already fixed it: Supplier A, model 1, a filter head with a patented latch: the spray face comes off with a two-finger pinch and the cartridge is out in under 5 seconds, no tools. Adoption: change of supplier · high confidence.
caso.chamfer.brief.traduccion: In English: “Write ONE implementation of the logic (CSS + JS) and use it the same way in demo.html and in the .liquid file. The demo swaps the Liquid values for sample content, nothing else.”
